topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: What is the Torrens system, as established under Minnesota Statutes Chapter 508?
choice_a: A mandatory statewide requirement that every deed be re-recorded every ten years
choice_b: A private title insurance program administered by the Minnesota Department of Commerce
choice_c: A federal program that replaced county recording offices with a single state registry
choice_d: A court-supervised system of land title registration that produces a certificate of title, offered as an alternative to the traditional abstract-and-opinion method of evidencing title
explanation: Chapter 508 ("Registration of Land") creates the Torrens registration system, under which an owner petitions the district court to have title examined and registered. Once registered, a certificate of title is issued and maintained by the registrar of titles, offering an alternative to relying on an abstract of title and attorney's opinion.
source_note: Minn. Stat. Ch. 508 (Registration of Land / Torrens system), e.g. 508.01, 508.03, 508.10 (live-verified at revisor.mn.gov)

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 508.25, what is the general legal effect of a Torrens certificate of title held by the registered owner?
choice_a: The owner holds the land free from all encumbrances and adverse claims except those specifically noted on the certificate or otherwise excepted by statute (such as unrecorded short-term leases, tax liens, and public highway rights)
choice_b: The certificate is only prima facie evidence of title and can be defeated by any unrecorded claim, the same as an abstract property
choice_c: The certificate guarantees the property is free of all liens with no exceptions whatsoever
choice_d: The certificate expires and must be renewed every five years or the land reverts to unregistered status
explanation: Minn. Stat. 508.25 provides that the holder of a certificate of title takes the land free from all encumbrances and adverse claims except those noted on the certificate itself and a short list of statutory exceptions, including certain unrecordable federal claims, real property tax and special assessment liens, short-term leases of three years or less with actual occupancy, and public highway rights.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Can title to registered (Torrens) land in Minnesota be acquired by adverse possession?
choice_a: Yes, using the same statutory period that applies to unregistered abstract land
choice_b: No; Minn. Stat. 508.02 provides that registered land is not subject to acquisition by adverse possession
choice_c: Yes, but only if the adverse possessor also pays the delinquent property taxes
choice_d: Only if the adverse possessor records a claim with the county recorder within one year
explanation: Minn. Stat. 508.02 states that while registered land generally has the same incidents as unregistered land, it is not subject to adverse possession — protecting the reliability of the certificate of title as the definitive record of ownership.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: In a Minnesota Torrens registration proceeding, what is the role of the "examiner of titles" created under Minn. Stat. 508.12?
choice_a: The county sheriff responsible for physically surveying the property boundaries
choice_b: A licensed real estate broker who certifies the fair market value of the property for tax purposes
choice_c: A court-appointed official who examines the abstract and evidence of title in a registration proceeding and reports findings and recommendations to the district court
choice_d: The buyer's attorney who drafts the purchase agreement
explanation: Minn. Stat. 508.12 establishes examiners of titles, who review the application, abstract, and supporting evidence in a land registration proceeding and report their findings and recommendations to the district court, which then determines whether to enter a decree of registration.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 287.035, what is the Minnesota Mortgage Registry Tax generally imposed on?
choice_a: The full purchase price of the property regardless of financing
choice_b: The buyer's gross annual income at a flat 2% rate
choice_c: The appraised value of the property at a rate of 1%
choice_d: The debt, or portion of a debt, secured by a mortgage of real property recorded in Minnesota, at a rate of 0.23% (0.0023) of the amount secured
explanation: Minn. Stat. 287.035 imposes the mortgage registry tax on the debt, or portion of a debt, secured by a mortgage of Minnesota real property that is presented for recording, at a rate of 0.23% (0.0023) of the secured debt amount.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Who is generally responsible for paying the Minnesota Mortgage Registry Tax when a mortgage is recorded?
choice_a: The mortgagor (borrower), since the tax is levied on the privilege of recording the mortgage that secures the borrower's debt
choice_b: The county recorder's office, out of general tax revenue
choice_c: The mortgagee (lender) exclusively, with no exceptions
choice_d: The real estate licensee who represented the buyer in the transaction
explanation: Under Minn. Stat. 287.035, the mortgage registry tax is assessed on the debt secured by the recorded mortgage, and the mortgagor is responsible for paying it in order to record the mortgage, though the parties may agree otherwise by contract.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 287.21, at what rate is the Minnesota Deed Tax generally imposed on a conveyance where the consideration exceeds $3,000?
choice_a: 1.5% of the appraised property value
choice_b: 0.33% (0.0033) of the net consideration for the conveyance
choice_c: A flat $500 regardless of consideration
choice_d: 0.23% of the loan amount used to finance the purchase
explanation: Minn. Stat. 287.21 imposes the deed tax on instruments conveying Minnesota real property at a rate of 0.33% (0.0033) of the net consideration when that consideration exceeds $3,000; conveyances at or below $3,000 (or certain exempt transfers) are instead subject to a flat $1.65 tax.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 287.21, what deed tax generally applies to a conveyance where the consideration is $3,000 or less?
choice_a: No deed tax is ever due below $3,000
choice_b: 0.33% of the assessed value regardless of the sale price
choice_c: A flat $1.65 deed tax
choice_d: A flat $100 minimum tax
explanation: Minn. Stat. 287.21 sets a flat $1.65 deed tax for conveyances with consideration of $3,000 or less, as well as for certain consolidations, mergers, and designated transfers, rather than applying the 0.33% percentage rate used for higher-value transfers.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 287.24, who is liable for paying the Minnesota Deed Tax on a conveyance?
choice_a: The grantee (buyer), as a condition of taking title
choice_b: The real estate licensees involved, split equally between listing and buyer's agents
choice_c: The county in which the property is located, from its general fund
choice_d: The person who grants, assigns, transfers, or conveys the real property (the grantor/seller), not the grantee
explanation: Minn. Stat. 287.24 provides that the person who grants, assigns, transfers, or conveys real property by a taxable deed or instrument is liable for the deed tax — meaning the seller/grantor, not the buyer, bears the statutory tax obligation (though the parties may allocate it differently by contract).

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minnesota's statutory new-home warranties (Minn. Stat. 327A.02), how long is the warranty against faulty workmanship and defective materials due to noncompliance with building standards?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Two years
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: Ten years
explanation: Minn. Stat. 327A.02, subd. 1, requires the vendor of a new dwelling to warrant, for one year, that the dwelling is free from defects caused by faulty workmanship and defective materials due to noncompliance with building standards.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 327A.02, what is the statutory warranty period covering faulty installation of the plumbing, electrical, heating, and cooling systems in a new dwelling?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Two years
choice_c: Six months
choice_d: Ten years
explanation: Minn. Stat. 327A.02, subd. 1, sets a two-year statutory warranty against defects caused by faulty installation of a new dwelling's plumbing, electrical, heating, and cooling systems — longer than the one-year workmanship/materials warranty but shorter than the ten-year major structural defect warranty.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 327A.02, how long does the statutory warranty against major construction defects due to noncompliance with building standards last for a new dwelling?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Two years
choice_c: Ten years
choice_d: Twenty years
explanation: Minn. Stat. 327A.02, subd. 1, provides the longest statutory warranty — ten years — for major construction defects caused by noncompliance with applicable building standards, reflecting the seriousness of structural defects compared to workmanship or systems defects.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 327A.02, what happens to the statutory home warranties if the original vendor or contractor later dissolves as a corporation or LLC, or the home is resold before the warranty period expires?
choice_a: The warranties automatically terminate the moment title passes to a new owner
choice_b: The warranties transfer only if the original buyer pays an additional transfer fee to the contractor
choice_c: The warranties become void if the contractor dissolves, with no recourse for the homeowner
choice_d: The warranties survive the passing of legal or equitable title to a subsequent buyer and remain enforceable even if the contractor later dissolves
explanation: Minn. Stat. 327A.02 specifies that the statutory warranties survive the passing of legal or equitable title to the dwelling and remain enforceable against the vendor or contractor even if that entity later dissolves as a corporation or limited liability company, protecting subsequent owners within the warranty periods.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under the Minnesota Human Rights Act (Minn. Stat. 363A.09), which protected classes for real property transactions go beyond those covered by the federal Fair Housing Act?
choice_a: Sexual orientation, marital status, gender identity, and status with regard to public assistance
choice_b: Race, color, and national origin
choice_c: Religion and familial status only
choice_d: Disability and sex only
explanation: Minn. Stat. 363A.09 prohibits discrimination in real property transactions based on the federal categories (race, color, creed/religion, national origin, sex, disability, familial status) plus Minnesota-added categories: sexual orientation, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, and gender identity — extending protection beyond federal Fair Housing Act law.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 363A.09, does the Minnesota Human Rights Act's prohibition on housing discrimination apply to real estate brokers and salespersons, in addition to property owners and lessors?
choice_a: No; the Act only regulates individual property owners, not licensees
choice_b: Yes; subdivision 2 specifically addresses discriminatory conduct by real estate brokers, salespersons, and their agents in real property transactions
choice_c: No; brokers are regulated exclusively under federal law and are exempt from the state Act
choice_d: Yes, but only for commercial property transactions, not residential
explanation: Minn. Stat. 363A.09, subd. 2, extends the Act's fair-housing prohibitions specifically to real estate brokers, salespersons, and their agents, in addition to subdivision 1's coverage of owners and lessees and subdivision 4's prohibition on discriminatory steering practices.
source_note: Minn. Stat. 363A.09, subd. 2, subd. 4 (live-verified at revisor.mn.gov)

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 363A.09, does the Minnesota Human Rights Act's real property discrimination provisions extend to lenders providing real estate financing?
choice_a: No; mortgage lending is governed only by federal law under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act
choice_b: No; the Act applies only to sales and leasing transactions, not financing
choice_c: Yes; subdivision 3 prohibits discriminatory practices by financial institutions in connection with real estate-related lending
choice_d: Yes, but only for loans originated by state-chartered banks, not credit unions
explanation: Minn. Stat. 363A.09, subd. 3, prohibits financial institutions from discriminating in the provision of real estate-related financing on the basis of the Act's protected classes, paralleling the federal Fair Housing Act's coverage of lending discrimination but under Minnesota's broader list of protected classes.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minnesota's Statute of Frauds (Minn. Stat. 513.04), which conveyances of an interest in land are exempt from the general requirement that such conveyances be in writing?
choice_a: All conveyances regardless of duration must be in writing, with no exceptions
choice_b: Leases of five years or less
choice_c: Any transfer where the parties are related by blood or marriage
choice_d: Leases of one year or less
explanation: Minn. Stat. 513.04 requires that a conveyance of an interest in land be in writing, subject to a narrow exception for leases for a term not exceeding one year, which may be created without a written instrument.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 513.05, what does Minnesota's Statute of Frauds require regarding contracts for the sale of land?
choice_a: A contract for the sale of land, or an interest in land, must be in writing and signed by the party to be charged, or it is void
choice_b: Land sale contracts may be entered into orally as long as there is a witness present
choice_c: Only contracts involving commercial property need be in writing; residential sale contracts may be oral
choice_d: A land sale contract need only be in writing if the purchase price exceeds $500,000
explanation: Minn. Stat. 513.05 provides that every contract for the leasing of land for more than one year, or for the sale of land or an interest in land, is void unless the contract, or a memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the party to be charged.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 115.55, when must a seller of property served by an Individual Sewage Treatment System (ISTS/septic system) provide the required written disclosure regarding the system?
choice_a: Only after closing, within 30 days of the buyer taking possession
choice_b: Before the purchase agreement is signed
choice_c: Disclosure is optional unless the buyer specifically requests it in writing
choice_d: At the time the deed is recorded with the county recorder
explanation: Minn. Stat. 115.55 requires a seller of real property served by an individual sewage treatment system to disclose in writing, before signing the purchase agreement, whether the sewage goes to a facility permitted by the Pollution Control Agency or whether it does not (in which case additional disclosures about the noncompliant system are required).

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 115.55, how long is a compliance inspection certificate valid for an existing Individual Sewage Treatment System, absent a public health threat?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Five years
choice_c: Three years
choice_d: Indefinitely, with no expiration
explanation: Minn. Stat. 115.55 provides that a compliance inspection certificate for an existing individual sewage treatment system generally remains valid for three years (compared to five years for a newly constructed or replaced system), unless a public health threat is discovered that shortens that period.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 115.55, what is the statute of limitations for a buyer to sue a seller who knowingly failed to disclose noncompliance of an Individual Sewage Treatment System?
choice_a: Six years
choice_b: Ten years
choice_c: There is no limitations period; a claim may be brought at any time
choice_d: Two years
explanation: Minn. Stat. 115.55 imposes liability on a seller who knowingly fails to disclose required ISTS compliance information, for the buyer's compliance costs and reasonable attorney fees, subject to a two-year statute of limitations — a shorter period than the six-year limitations period that applies to nondisclosure claims under the separate well disclosure statute.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 103I.235, when must a seller of Minnesota real property provide the required written well disclosure to the buyer?
choice_a: Before signing the purchase agreement
choice_b: Only if the buyer requests a title search
choice_c: Within one year after closing
choice_d: Disclosure is required only for agricultural properties
explanation: Minn. Stat. 103I.235 requires that before signing a purchase agreement to sell real property, the seller must disclose in writing to the buyer information about the status and location of any wells on the property, either by certifying that no wells exist or by providing a disclosure statement describing each well.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 103I.235, what document must generally be provided at closing if wells exist on the property being sold?
choice_a: A certified well-water test report from a state-licensed laboratory dated within 24 hours of closing
choice_b: A well disclosure certificate, signed by the seller or an authorized representative, containing the well status information plus the buyer's name and mailing address and the well's location by quartile, section, township, and range
choice_c: Nothing further is required beyond the initial purchase agreement disclosure
choice_d: A bond posted with the county recorder equal to the cost of sealing all wells on the property
explanation: Minn. Stat. 103I.235 requires that, at the time of closing, the seller provide a well disclosure certificate containing the disclosure information, the buyer's name and mailing address, and the location of each well by quartile, section, township, and range, signed by the seller or an authorized representative; if no wells exist, a certification statement in the deed may substitute for a separate certificate.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 103I.235, which of the following transactions is exempt from the well disclosure requirement?
choice_a: The sale of a single-family home with a well currently in use
choice_b: The sale of vacant residential land with a sealed well
choice_c: The sale of an individual condominium unit
choice_d: The sale of a duplex where one well serves both units
explanation: Minn. Stat. 103I.235 exempts certain transactions from the well disclosure requirement, including sales of individual condominium units, sales of severed mineral interests only, and sales involving only temporary borings or unsuccessful wells that have already been sealed by a licensed contractor.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 103I.235, within how many years after the sale may a buyer sue a seller who knowingly failed to disclose a well as required?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Two years
choice_c: There is no limitations period
choice_d: Six years
explanation: Minn. Stat. 103I.235 makes a seller who knowingly fails to disclose required well information liable for the buyer's well-sealing costs and reasonable attorney fees if the buyer brings suit within six years of the purchase — notably longer than the two-year limitations period under the parallel ISTS/septic disclosure statute.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: What is the general purpose of Minnesota's Petroleum Tank Release Cleanup Act, Minn. Stat. Ch. 115C?
choice_a: It establishes a regulatory and funding framework — including the Petroleum Tank Release Compensation Board and Petroleum Tank Fund — for responding to and reimbursing costs of cleaning up releases from leaking underground petroleum storage tanks
choice_b: It sets construction standards for new above-ground swimming pools
choice_c: It requires all real estate licensees to carry petroleum spill insurance
choice_d: It governs the licensing of real estate appraisers who inspect gas stations
explanation: Minn. Stat. Ch. 115C addresses petroleum tank releases, creating the Petroleum Tank Release Compensation Board and Petroleum Tank Fund to help responsible parties fund the response to, and cleanup of, releases from underground storage tanks such as leaking petroleum tanks, which is directly relevant to real property affected by contamination.

topic: Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties
question: Under Minn. Stat. 115C.09, what may an eligible party seeking to clean up a leaking underground petroleum storage tank on real property generally obtain?
choice_a: An automatic property tax exemption for the affected parcel
choice_b: Reimbursement from the Petroleum Tank Fund for eligible corrective action costs
choice_c: A waiver of the deed tax on the property's next sale
choice_d: Immunity from all future environmental liability regardless of future acts
explanation: Minn. Stat. 115C.09 sets out the reimbursement process under which eligible parties responding to a petroleum tank release may recover eligible cleanup costs from the Petroleum Tank Fund, subject to statutory deductibles and caps, with an appeals process for reimbursement determinations under 115C.12.
